disposition: PASS conditional on the separately bound preceding normalized model; terminal thirteen-step calculation verified on the actual mixed-characteristic stalk. No Lean elaboration run.
derivation: With w²=-2L, the half-root equations have positive right sides w^6/L^3 and 2401*w^6/L^3. The Rees equations before each of the first three blowups have exponent 6,4,2: w and S directions cover by taking homogeneous primes and forcing both A and B. In each proposed chart, modulo scale, 2 times an inverted unit is a nonzerodivisor and the remaining two equations are separate monics. Regular sequence permutation in the localized ambient rings puts scale last. Thus ratios embed in the localization, with no extra vertical divisor. On S charts the two derivatives are 1 and on w charts they are S, so at every prime except S=0 the special divisor is etale over a regular base. At S=0 the sole residue prime has A=B=0,0,1 in the successive w charts. This argument concerns all primes, not just rational directions.

At the last origin, w is regular in the one-root ring C and C/(w)=F2[A,A^-1], via S=A^-1-A. Thus C_q is regular of dimension 2 and T=C_q[e]_(w,A-1,e) regular of dimension 3. Independent expansion with g=G/A² gives (1+d)^2+(g-1)(1+d)-2401g=d²+(g+1)d-2400g. Substituting d=e+2400 gives e(e+1+g+4800)+2400*2401. Since w^10=-32 L^5, ev=(75*2401/L^5)w^10 and the coefficient is a unit at residue characteristic two. The inverse B=A(2401+e) shows this is the same hypersurface, without adjoining an independent v.

Writing p=A-1 gives t=w modulo m², because 2 lies in m², A^-2 and the constant of L^-3 reduce to 1 there. Hence e,v,p are parameters by the nonsingular tangent change v=e+w. In T/(e,v), a DVR with parameter p, first w is in p², so 2 is in p⁴. With v=e=0 the unit equation L³ A²=-1/4801 follows exactly; its right side minus 1 is -4802/4801 and vanishes mod p³. Write w=c p²; L=1+w mod p³ and A²=1+p² mod p³. The resulting coefficient of p² is c+1 in F2. Therefore c is a unit and lifts to a unit gamma in T, with w=alpha*e+beta*v+gamma*p². This is an ordinary local-ring argument, not a completion or tangent-only guess.

For each ordinary surface blowup in the ambient regular threefold, scale s is regular, ambient chart mod s is polynomial on two ratios over the old residue field, and the divided hypersurface is not the zero polynomial there. Reducing sr=a f' modulo s forces a divisible by s and proves scale regular on the quotient; localization recovers the old surface with s inverted. Consequently the proposed quotient equals the actual ratio chart. In the first two crossing blowups each e- or v-direction has linear exceptional divisor; the p chart has crossing E_i V_i=0, regular apart from its sole origin. Pullbacks give w=p Z1 then w=p² Z2 with Z2(0)=gamma nonzero. Directly dividing ev=H w^10 by p^4 leaves X Y=p^16 H Z2^10; the unit restriction is needed only near the remaining origin, others already regular.

Every remaining k>2 blowup of XY=p^k*D has two linear exceptional charts and one crossing with decrement 2; 16 to 2 takes seven. At k=2 the conic XY=delta P² is smooth over F2 including geometric points: singularity would require X=Y=0, forcing P=0. Chartwise the X/Y charts solve linearly and the P chart has invertible X and Y. The nonzero exceptional chart equations imply the same saturation argument through the final blowup. This accounts for all thirteen ordinary centers. Their closed F2 origins are global closed points of successive exceptional fibres; local base change controls every affected stalk, with unchanged complements. The identified proper integral global model remains flat over Z by torsion-freeness.
